key_insight: Coarse-mesh graph neural networks predict sparse flow observables without reconstructing solver-resolution states, matching or outperforming finer-mesh surrogates at lower cost.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers efficient prediction of local measurements and integrated quantities for flow monitoring, system identification, and state estimation.
method: Train parameterized GNN surrogates directly on coarse meshes.
Select training conditions adaptively using frequency-spectrum variations.
Use noise-augmented multi-step unrolling to improve long-horizon autoregressive predictions.
evidence_signal: Tests on parameterized 2D/3D confined cylinder flows and an unevenly heated cavity showed generalization to unseen conditions; adaptive sampling reduced maximum errors by an order of magnitude versus uniform sampling.
watch_item: Generalization beyond the tested flow configurations and parameter ranges remains unestablished.
paper_title: Predicting Sparse Observables in Parameterized Unsteady Flows Using Coarse-Mesh Graph Neural Networks
